findings.title: Codex response-reader facts are combined across separate commands
findings.observation: Cycle 6 requires the exact response filename somewhere in shellArguments(call.command), while jq and requestId are also tested against the complete multi-line call. It does not prove that the jq command producing the parsed request ID actually reads that response file.
findings.trigger: Use one exec call whose first line runs jq against unrelated-replay-response.json and returns the authoritative claim request ID, while a second independent line only runs test -f replay-response.json.
findings.impact: The verifier returns PASS even though the request ID was not read from the successful replay response. Facts from separate commands can still be assembled into a false compatibility record, violating AC-15 and the documented exact response-file read gate.

evidence.description: At the exact head, a temporary negative used jq against unrelated-replay-response.json followed by test -f replay-response.json in the same exec call. The assertion failed because verifyClientEvidence resolved PASS with every Codex objective.
evidence.reference: reviewer cross-command response-reader counterexample at ba6e3aac48d0c724414620a3077a4e1284303cf7

evidence.description: Response readers are selected using arguments, jq presence and requestId presence over the whole command string, not the same parsed command segment.
Any matching request ID in the whole exec output is combined with the replay request path/status and accepted by claim matching.
Cycle 6 covers the exact longer-filename alias but not a multi-line exec where jq and the expected filename occur in different commands.
The real Codex record passes, and the SHA-bound 206-line Claude transcript prefix also passes. The failure is specifically exact response-file identity, not positive-evidence availability.
AC-15 requires each named client to actually execute the representative validation, and the plan disallows a hand-written assertion without live request/resource correlation.

findings.remediation: Bind jq, its requestId selector, the exact successful replay response-file input and the corresponding output to the same parsed command segment. Do not combine predicates or arguments across separate newline/pipeline/compound-command segments. Add the cross-command negative while preserving all current alias, request-ID, status, cross-operation, body/key and live-resource checks.
findings.verification: Both current real client records still pass; all existing negatives remain closed; and a multi-line exec with jq reading unrelated-replay-response.json plus a separate test -f replay-response.json fails with CLIENT_EVIDENCE_COMMITTED_TRANSCRIPT.

findings.title: Child-resource writes are committed without matching public reads
findings.observation: The current implementation maps every scenario result ref to a direct or paginated public read and requires an exact ID match.
findings.trigger: A normal, recovered or terminal-replayed journal entry contains a child resource reference.
findings.impact: The exact child must be publicly present before COMMITTED/PASS; missing or mismatched children now fail closed.

evidence.description: Exact report/progress reads pass, mismatched progress fails, and terminal replay performs zero writes while reading reports and progress.

findings.verification: Targeted unit tests and exact-head CI verify normal, recovery and terminal readback behavior.

findings.title: IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS is persisted as terminal rejection
findings.observation: The current recovery helper recognizes the bounded retry contract, preserves exact bytes/key and leaves exhaustion OUTCOME_UNKNOWN.
findings.trigger: Recovery receives one or more 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS responses.
findings.impact: Temporary concurrency no longer becomes terminal local rejection and the original intent remains resumable.

evidence.description: The exact-head regression proves retry-success after two sends and OUTCOME_UNKNOWN after three bounded in-progress responses, with identical body and key.

findings.verification: Targeted unit tests and exact-head CI pass.

required_actions.action: Bind jq, its exact response-file input and parsed request-ID output to one command segment; add the multi-line cross-command negative.
Publicly reconcile each exact child resource before COMMITTED/PASS and on terminal replay.
Implement and test bounded IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS recovery with frozen bytes and key.

limitations: Reviewer-local npm was 11.12.1 rather than the declared 11.16.0; exact configured-runtime authority comes from successful exact-head GitHub CI.
A fresh-context independent sub-agent pass was unavailable under the active no-delegation policy; the Review task performed a separate full/delta pass and executable adversarial reproduction.

Client transcript provenance is operator-observed rather than cryptographically attested; the validator must therefore make every checkable client/authority correlation exact.
